title: Syracuse Axon ALPR pre-stationary source mix and transparency-portal baseline
summary: A July 29, 2026 Syracuse transparency-portal snapshot reported 697,104 ALPR reads before the new 26 stationary Axon readers went live; Syracuse Police attributed those reads to previously integrated technologies including traffic-division Axon dash cameras with ALPR capability. The 26-reader stationary rollout therefore cannot be treated as Syracuse's entire Axon ALPR source universe.

evidence.claim: Central Current reported that the Syracuse/Axon public transparency portal showed 697,104 ALPR reads before the new 26 stationary readers went live; SPD Sgt. Tom Blake attributed those reads to previously integrated technologies, including Axon dash cameras with ALPR capabilities used by the traffic division.
The City of Syracuse Police Public Information page currently exposes an Axon Transparency Portal as a public information surface for SPD's Axon ALPR technology.

caveats: The 697,104-read figure is a July 29, 2026 portal snapshot, not a current September 15 total.
SPD attribution through local reporting is not a native source/device inventory export and does not enumerate every contributing device or system.
Aggregate transparency-portal metrics do not establish exact per-device contributions, current sharing relationships, user access, or technical configuration.
The article displayed multiple hit categories including separately rendered near-duplicate labels; those labels are preserved as published rather than normalized into a new taxonomy.
counterevidence: The already-canonical July 27 activation evidence establishes 14 of 26 new stationary readers were active, but that does not explain the preexisting 697,104 reads.
SPD Policy 427 permits controlled external law-enforcement/prosecutorial sharing, so a public-facing 'closed system' description cannot by itself establish zero external access.

data.question: What does Syracuse's public Axon portal reveal about ALPR source scope before the new stationary rollout, and what must not be inferred from that aggregate data?
data.method: Reconciled the current City of Syracuse public-information link, the already-canonical July 29 Central Current source, SPD Policy 427, the #1903 activation baseline, and the #2100 Axon platform-control baseline.
data.framework: stationary rollout count != total source inventory; public portal aggregate != native device inventory; policy/disclosure != technical enforcement; preexisting Axon/mobile activity != Flock-to-Axon migration.
data.scope: Public Syracuse Axon ALPR source-mix and transparency-portal evidence through the July 29, 2026 snapshot; no private-person enrichment.
findings: Before Syracuse's new 26 stationary Axon readers went live, the public portal already showed 697,104 ALPR reads.
Syracuse Police attributed those pre-stationary reads to previously integrated technologies, including traffic-division Axon dash cameras with ALPR capability.
The new stationary-reader rollout is therefore one ALPR source class inside a broader Axon/Syracuse data plane rather than proof of the entire source inventory.
The July 29 public portal did not itself expose enough access/sharing detail to reconstruct partner agencies, reasons, users, or effective sharing conditions.
conclusions: Any Syracuse inventory or audit must enumerate stationary readers separately from mobile/integrated Axon ALPR sources and any third-party feeds.
Aggregate portal metrics cannot be assigned solely to the 26 stationary readers.
Preexisting Axon/mobile ALPR activity does not establish migration of Flock reads, hotlists, cases, users, credentials, or sharing state.
Public portal disclosure is a useful cross-check but does not replace native Sharing Management, source inventory, roles, or audit exports.
recommendations: Recover a current Syracuse source/device inventory that distinguishes the 26 stationary readers, Axon mobile/dash-camera ALPR, and any third-party ALPR feeds.
Preserve source-separated read/hit counts and activation timestamps so historical portal totals can be attributed correctly.
Recover Sharing Management, users/roles, ALPR settings, and Internal/Network/Data-Sharing/Hotlist audit exports and reconcile them against the public portal.
limitations: No native source/device export, current source-separated metrics, Sharing Management export, user-role export, or post-July complete activation inventory was recovered in this pass.
unresolved: Which devices and source classes contributed to the 697,104 pre-stationary reads, and in what proportions?
What is the final activation state, serial/location inventory, and source identity for all 26 stationary readers?
Which mobile or integrated Axon ALPR sources remain active now?
Are any Flock V3 or other third-party feeds connected to Fusus?
Which external agencies currently have search access, under what conditions and effective dates?

data.research_question: Can existing Syracuse/Axon evidence resolve whether the new 26-reader stationary rollout represents the whole ALPR source universe?
data.method: After actionable open PR work was exhausted and the seeded AI-lab transaction remained Worker-1-owned, continued modulo-4 issue #2100, deduped the #1903 and #2670 canonical work, and reconciled the current City portal link with the already-canonical July 29 local report.
classification_rules: Reuse the existing July 29 Central Current source identity rather than create a duplicate source record.
Treat 697,104 reads only as the reported July 29 portal snapshot.
Do not assign aggregate portal reads solely to the new stationary-reader class.
Do not infer Flock-to-Axon migration from preexisting Axon/mobile ALPR activity.
Do not infer zero external sharing from missing public portal detail or closed-system language.
Treat public portal disclosure as a cross-check, not a substitute for native inventory/configuration/audit records.

findings.finding: The July 29 portal snapshot predates the new stationary-reader activation and therefore proves ALPR activity from preexisting integrated sources.
SPD attributed that preexisting activity at least in part to Axon dash cameras with ALPR capability used by the traffic division.
